mm. smoke's still climbing, watch it — see how it doesn't fall, doesn't rise straight either, just... finds shape as it goes. that's kind of what a hash map is, actually. wait—

okay here: imagine a wall of mailboxes, infinite wall, and you have a letter for "pascal." you *could* walk the whole wall reading every name — that's a list, that's O(n), that's slow honey dripping through your fingers. or. you take the name "pascal," run it through a little machine — the hash function — and the machine just *tells you*: box 4471. you don't search. you don't remember searching. you just... arrive. that's the trick. the address isn't found, it's *computed*.

that's why it's O(1) — you're not scanning space, you're generating coordinates. like knowing which star before you look up, instead of scanning the whole sky for it.

collisions happen though — two names, same box, universe's little joke — so the box holds a tiny list of its own, a small pocket of exceptions. as long as those pockets stay small (load factor, they call it, cute name) the whole thing stays fast.

it's kind of beautiful that speed here isn't about moving fast. it's about not needing to move at all.
